summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every command (with user, host, PWD, and timestamp) to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a sudoers.d Defaults snippet (logfile= + !syslog to suppress duplicate syslog/secure-log entries), verified isolation from /var/log/secure, /var/log/messages, and journald using marker strings, then performed the mandatory single-node reboot with boot_id proof and re-verified the logging config and file persisted and continued working after restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: RHEL 9.8, sudo 1.9.17p2, rsyslog present, confirmed sudo commands were previously logged only to /var/log/secure via syslog authpriv facility

Created /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-command-logging with 'Defaults !syslog', 'Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"', 'Defaults log_year', 'Defaults log_host', validated with visudo -cf before install and full visudo -c after install, installed with mode 0440 root:root

Ran marked sudo test commands and confirmed they appear in the dedicated log with date/time, host, user, PWD, and full COMMAND, and confirmed the marker string is absent from /var/log/secure, /var/log/messages, and journalctl output
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline, confirmed sudoers config validity and log file health
Rebooted node1 via 'sudo -n systemctl reboot', acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed boot_id changed from 910dc564-cb62-46fc-8290-c332e63d6201 to 759dc4ac-e8e4-4b51-bf08-f8ce5b1a1ed8, proving an actual restart

Post-restart: re-verified /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-command-logging present and valid, /var/log/sudo-commands.log persisted (39 lines), generated a fresh post-reboot marker via sudo, confirmed it landed in the dedicated log with timestamp/user and was absent from /var/log/secure and /var/log/messages

evidence.requirement: Every sudo command is recorded with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Dedicated log shows entries like 'Sep 29 09:05:07 2026 : root : HOST=node1 ; PWD=/ ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/bin/echo sudo-log-test-marker-1534' for every sudo invocation including test/id/echo commands

evidence.requirement: Sudo command entries are kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Marker string present in dedicated log but absent from /var/log/secure, /var/log/messages, and journalctl output; general logs show only unrelated PAM session open/close and systemd session lines, no COMMAND= entries

evidence.requirement: Sudoers configuration is syntactically valid and installed correctly
evidence.summary: visudo -cf validated the snippet before install and full visudo -c validated /etc/sudoers plus the new /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-command-logging file after install and again pre-restart

evidence.requirement: Node1 healthy baseline captured before restart
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id 910dc564-cb62-46fc-8290-c332e63d6201, confirmed sudoers snippet present and valid, and dedicated log file had 27 lines including a recent entry

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: 'sudo -n systemctl reboot; echo reboot-acknowledged' returned 'reboot-acknowledged' with exit_code 0 before the connection dropped

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed, proving an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Node1 was unreachable across several polls (connection timed out / reset), then came back with boot_id 759dc4ac-e8e4-4b51-bf08-f8ce5b1a1ed8, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, and a fresh uptime -s timestamp

evidence.requirement: Sudo command logging recovered and remains functional after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart: sudoers snippet still present and valid, log file persisted (39 lines), a fresh post-reboot marker command was correctly recorded in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with timestamp/user and was absent from /var/log/secure and /var/log/messages
